Gaps in screenshots, screen recording and the capture pipeline.

- Screen recording records the focused output or an area with `wf-recorder`, encoded as H.264 by VA-API, else NVENC, else libx264 on the CPU (`recording.encoder`); one that cannot start gives way to libx264 once, and the log and `kanade capture record status` say so. The quality (`recording.quality`) is a fixed quantizer, so a busy screen makes a large file. The encoder flags have been checked with `ffmpeg` and GStreamer on test video, not yet through `wf-recorder` on a live screen. niri hands out a frame only when the screen changes, so a still screen records few frames, and each resumed segment waits for its first frame.
- Recording sound is none, the system's or the microphone's, one at a time (no mix). The microphone is recorded only when you choose it for that start. The audio uses the default output's monitor and the default input, as the sound server names them; this has not been checked against a live `wf-recorder`.
- A recording is written to its file from the first frame, so one you never pause is finished at that name, even if Kanade or the machine dies (the recorder ends with it). A window recording is written as a fragmented mp4, a fragment each second, so a death leaves a file that plays up to about the last second. Pausing ends a segment; the segments after the first go in a hidden folder beside the file, `.Screencast from <stamp>.parts/`, and stopping joins them with `ffmpeg` (copying, no re-encode; the island says Saving meanwhile, and the file's name is free for that time). How well the picture and sound stay in step across the joins has not been checked. If the join fails, or Kanade or the machine dies after a resume, the file holds the first segment and the folder the rest, or, if the death came during the join, the final name is absent and the folder holds every segment, the first included, and maybe a partial `.joined.mp4` (Kanade never deletes the folder, and the failure says where it is); join them by hand or delete the folder. Killed while paused and not resumed, the file holds everything. Saving never replaces a file: if one appeared at the name, the recording stays in the folder. A long join can take over 5 seconds, so `stop` may say it is unknown while the file still lands.
- Locking the session while recording stops and saves the recording; a start or resume is refused while locked. Choosing an area needs `slurp`; there is no overlay of Kanade's own for it yet. See [ADR 0013](https://github.com/0x1d1e/kanade/blob/main/docs/adr/0013-screen-recording-with-wf-recorder.md).
- Recording a window needs `gst-launch-1.0` with the PipeWire plugin and that of the chosen encoder (VA-API, NVENC or x264), and `ffmpeg`; niri casts DMA-BUF only, which VA-API takes directly; NVENC and x264 take it through VA-API's post-processor, so on a machine without a working VA-API driver (NVIDIA-only) they fall back to EGL, which fails on Intel's compressed tiled buffers and is not verified elsewhere, and a window may then not record (`kanade doctor` names the download and tries the chain on a test frame, not a live cast); a missing one fails the start and `kanade doctor` names it. The window keeps its size at start (a resize is letterboxed, not rescaled); sound and picture are stamped by arrival time and are not guaranteed to be in sync; a window on a scaled output is not verified. A window that closes ends the recording and saves what exists. A window scrolled out of view (an off-screen column, or not visible) gets no frames until it is visible again, and the chain ends after 3 s without a buffer, so such a take fails and walks the encoder fallback instead of waiting; the same happens to a window that has not repainted since the cast opened, and to a chain that wedges mid-take, whose reason names 3 s without a picture. A window that is merely still is not affected: niri's cast re-sends its last frame every second. A still window can still make `start` reach its 5 s budget (`no frame was written within 5s; it may still record`, exit 3) while the take runs on correctly. The playability of a window recording after `kill -9` of Kanade is checked on the encoder pipeline alone (synthetic source), not yet live on the real window pipeline. The window's cast shows in the privacy dots beside the Recording on the island (two dots for one recording), and Stop sharing in Controls ends niri's cast too; whether the recording is then saved is not verified (stop it with `kanade capture record stop` instead). If Kanade exits during a window recording, niri keeps the cast until a Kanade next starts, which stops it (a Kanade that is still running keeps its own). See [ADR 0117](https://github.com/0x1d1e/kanade/blob/main/docs/adr/0117-window-recording-through-nirs-screen-cast.md).
- Changing what a share shows (`kanade capture cast`) works only for a cast with a dynamic target, which a portal share picks by its own choice, and needs a niri with the `set-dynamic-cast-*` actions (26.04 has them); there is no button for it in the Capture Surface or Controls, only the verb, which a bind can run. The Controls header marks casts `(paused)` when every one has stopped streaming frames, but only for a cast that captures a window or a screen. See [ADR 0072](https://github.com/0x1d1e/kanade/blob/main/docs/adr/0072-dynamic-cast-target-verb.md).
- Stop sharing in Controls ends only a PipeWire screen cast (a browser or chat app sharing through the portal), through niri's `stop-cast` action, so it needs a niri that has it. niri cannot stop a `wlr-screencopy` cast, like `wf-recorder`'s, so that one has no button; stop it in its own program or the Capture Surface.
